comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find the evidence for Mecp2's dynamic expression during liver regeneration convincing and well-supported (C1, C29-C33, C40-C42). Both accept the temporal correlation with cell cycle markers.

Strong agreement on genetic manipulation experiments (C2-C5, C44-C47). Both find evidence for Mecp2's regulatory role in quiescence exit well-supported. Peer review encompasses additional claims (C6-C7, C48-C52, C54) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Partial overlap on overexpression experiments (C6, C48-C49). OpenEval finds AAV-mediated overexpression data supportive; peer review groups this with broader genetic manipulation evidence and finds it convincing.

Partial overlap on rescue experiments (C7, C50-C52). OpenEval emphasizes genetic complementation strengthening causality; peer review includes this in broader assessment of Mecp2's regulatory role as well-supported.

Partial agreement on generalizability across cell types (C55-C59 vs C57-C59). Both find in vitro evidence convincing. Peer review encompasses broader set of cell culture claims (C60-C66) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Partial overlap on 3T3 cell experiments (C60-C63). OpenEval finds siRNA knockdown data strongly supportive with quantitative evidence; peer review groups with broader cell culture systems and finds convincing.
Partial overlap on overexpression in 3T3 cells (C64, C66). OpenEval emphasizes bidirectional manipulation as strong support; peer review includes in broader cell culture evidence assessment.
Minimal overlap on control data (C65). OpenEval finds this important for showing specificity to proliferative signals; peer review implicitly accepts as part of broader cell culture evidence.

Significant disagreement. OpenEval finds proteasome-mediated degradation mechanism well-supported by convergent evidence (C8, C67-C71). Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the trigger for degradation remains unclear despite biochemical data.

Disagreement on Nedd4 functional evidence (C9, C72-C75). OpenEval finds bidirectional manipulation experiments supportive of functional link. Peer review remains uncertain about mechanistic connection between extrinsic signals and Nedd4 activation.

Disagreement on mechanistic understanding. OpenEval finds RNA-seq and ChIP-seq integration strongly supportive of direct target identification (C10, C76-C79, C86). Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, questioning how Mecp2 differentially regulates proliferation vs metabolic genes.

Agreement on uncertainty. Both find ChIP-seq data on stable occupancy (C80-C82) intriguing but lacking mechanistic explanation. OpenEval notes speculative interpretations; peer review questions differential regulation mechanism.

Agreement on nuclear receptor validation (C11-C13, C91-C92). Both find knockdown experiments supportive of functional relevance. OpenEval emphasizes phenocopy of Mecp2 loss; peer review accepts as downstream effectors.

Agreement on in vivo NR validation (C93-C96). Both find rescue experiments supportive though incomplete. OpenEval notes limited animal numbers; peer review acknowledges incomplete rescue suggests additional mechanisms.
Perfect agreement. Both find temporal specificity data (C53) supportive of Mecp2's role being limited to early regeneration/G0-G1 transition rather than later stages.
Partial overlap on differential NR expression (C83-C85). OpenEval finds qPCR data and inferences reasonable. Peer review groups with broader mechanistic questions about differential regulation.
Strong agreement on baseline characterization (C43, C105-C107). Both find evidence that cKO model lacks confounding pathology supportive, establishing specificity to regenerative response.
OpenEval rates morphological observation (C108) as UNCERTAIN due to speculative interpretation about mitosis attenuation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds RNA-seq data on metabolic gene dysregulation (C117) directly supported and consistent with proposed model. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

Agreement on inverse Mecp2-Ki67 relationship (C38-C39, C33). OpenEval emphasizes correlation supporting functional relationship; peer review implicitly accepts as part of convincing evidence for dual regulatory mechanism.

Partial overlap on integrated model (C98-C103 vs C98-C101). OpenEval finds model well-supported despite speculative elements. Peer review questions mechanistic basis for differential regulation, rating UNCERTAIN.
